transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Before we dive into the supplier early-payment program proposal, I want to make sure we've got our bases covered in the pre-authorization huddle. The draft as it stands uses the full $10 million submitted invoice pool, but I'm not seeing a quarterly cash cap, any guidance on accounting classification, or an invoice-exclusion control. I'd like to hear from procurement, treasury, and tax accounting on each of those gaps before I can sign off. Who'd like to start?

While reviewing supplier contracts, I identified $2,400,000 of invoices that are subject to public-procurement clauses prohibiting early-payment discounts. That means the eligible invoice pool is actually $7,600,000, not $10,000,000. Those restricted invoices must be excluded from the program. This directly addresses the invoice-exclusion control gap you raised — we need to build a control to screen out public-procurement-clause invoices before any suppliers are enrolled.

This memo has not yet been attached to the approval file, so I want to make sure it's formally incorporated before you sign off. Record supplier discounts as finance costs with a quarterly finance-cost reconciliation, and attach the tax-accounting memo to the approval file before sign-off.
